chain.title: Raw Logic Chip
chain.desc: A block of quartz, gold nuggets, redstone and a clay ball; the single component every other item in the mod is built from.

chain.title: Logic Chip
chain.desc: Smelt the raw chip. Set up a stack of these before you go further - a working LaserIO network eats them by the dozen.

chain.title: Laser Connector
chain.desc: Iron, glass, redstone and a Logic Chip. Place one on any inventory, machine or energy block; it is the socket the whole network plugs into.

chain.title: Laser Node
chain.desc: Iron and glass panes around a Laser Connector. Nodes hold the cards and link to connectors by line of sight, so there is no cable to route.

chain.title: Item Card
chain.desc: Gold nuggets, lapis, quartz and redstone around a Logic Chip. Slot it into a node's face and set it to Extract, Insert, Stock or Sensor - one card does all four jobs.

chain.title: Laser Wrench
chain.desc: Iron around a Logic Chip; it rotates nodes, copies a node's whole card layout and shows you where the beams are actually going.

chain.title: Basic Filter
chain.desc: Iron bars and glass panes around a Logic Chip; drop it into a card to whitelist or blacklist up to fifteen exact items.

chain.title: Card Holder
chain.desc: A chest and iron around a Logic Chip; it carries a stack of configured cards so you can build out a network without walking back to storage.

chain.title: Overclocker Card
chain.desc: Gold and redstone around a Logic Chip. Stack these into a card to raise how much it moves per tick, at the cost of more energy per operation.

chain.title: Energy Card
chain.desc: A redstone block, quartz, gold nuggets and redstone around a Logic Chip; it moves FE between connectors exactly the way the item card moves items.

chain.title: Fluid Card
chain.desc: The same shape with a bucket in it; fluids follow the same Extract/Insert/Stock/Sensor modes as everything else.

chain.title: Redstone Card
chain.desc: Quartz, gold nuggets and redstone around a Logic Chip; it reads and emits redstone across the network, turning the laser mesh into a signal bus.

chain.title: Count Filter
chain.desc: An observer plus a Basic Filter. It filters by exact stack counts, which is what makes a Stock card actually hold a target number in a machine.

chain.title: Tag Filter
chain.desc: Paper plus a Basic Filter; match by item tag instead of by item, so one card handles every ingot or every log at once.

chain.title: Mod Filter
chain.desc: A book plus a Basic Filter; match everything from a given mod, the fastest way to sort a mixed output stream by namespace.

chain.title: NBT Filter
chain.desc: White wool plus a Basic Filter; match on NBT so enchanted books, charged cells and damaged tools stop sharing a slot.

chain.title: Node Overclocker
chain.desc: Diamonds and redstone around a Logic Chip; where the card overclocker speeds one card, this speeds the whole node.

chain.title: Advanced Connector
chain.desc: Ender pearls, diamonds, gold and redstone around a basic Connector; it reaches much further and connects across chunk lines that stop the basic one.

chain.title: Card Cloner
chain.desc: Paper and iron around a Logic Chip; stamp one configured card and print copies of it, which is the only sane way to wire a large base.

notes: THE CARDS ARE THE CONTENT. LaserIO ships 19 items and 4 of them are infrastructure (raw chip, chip, connector, node); the other 15 are cards, filters and overclockers, and the mod's actual depth is in card CONFIGURATION - each card has four modes (Extract, Insert, Stock, Sensor), a channel colour, a priority, a round-robin toggle and a filter slot - none of which is a separate registered item. A quest chain therefore has to quest the cards and describe the modes, because there is no deeper item tier to reach for. All 19 items are quested here: 19 in the chain, all 19 across the three wheels. Nothing dropped - every id has a crafting or smelting recipe in data/laserio/recipes. VERIFICATION AND A CORRECTED OVERCOUNT: the naive models INTERSECT lang pass finds 29 item models but only 19 lang keys. The 10 extras (card_item_extract, card_item_stock, card_item_sensor and the same three each for fluid, energy plus card_redstone_extract) are NOT items - assets/laserio/models/item/card_item.json declares them as predicate overrides on 'laserio:mode', and each extra file is a one-line child model that only swaps layer1 to a different mode texture. Confirmed by reading the parent model. Pass 2 re-derived the id set independently from .class constant-pool strings, item textures, blockstates, recipe results and loot tables: all 19 corroborated, nothing missed. The mod also declares a hard dependency on patchouli and ships a guide book, but the book is a patchouli:guide_book with NBT rather than a laserio-namespaced item, so no manual id appears here. JAR SOURCE: LaserIO is not published on Modrinth - the only 1.20.1 Forge builds are on CurseForge (project 626839), and 1.6.8 (file 5074767, 2024-02-01) is the newest. CurseForge tags that file for both Forge and NeoForge on 1.20.1; META-INF/mods.toml is present and there is no fabric.mod.json, Java 17 class files, so it is a valid Forge jar. Its declared minecraft versionRange is the loose [1.18.2,) and pack_format is 9, which is normal for this multi-version single-jar mod and is not evidence of a wrong-version build - the CurseForge 1.20.1+Forge filter and the class-file version are what confirm it. NO CONSENSUS DATA: moddb.json has no laserio entry, so the ordering here is the recipe dependency graph alone (raw chip -> chip -> connector -> node -> cards, filters branching off filter_basic, advanced connector off basic).
